unit.why: A first-person memorate by the author of Megillat Setarim (R. Yitzhak Yehuda Yehiel of Komarno): as a nine-year-old at the Seer of Lublin's Passover seder, the Seer hesitated three times and then gave him the zeroa, followed by a kabbalistic explanation of his soul-root.

stories.summary_en: The author recalls visiting the Seer of Lublin with his father at age nine for Passover. He saw fire over the Seer's head. On the second seder night the Seer looked into the boy's soul-root, wavered three times, and then gave him the zeroa with trembling, as he usually did only for his great disciples. The author then explains this kabbalistically as the root of his soul in the Ari.
